# Northstar Historical Program Archive

## Archive purpose

This archive contains superseded proposals, workshop notes, and closed decisions retained for institutional context. It deliberately resembles current program material, but nothing in this file changes the approved facts in the program dossier, reliability manual, governance handbook, or delivery register. Readers must verify whether a date or owner is current before using it.

## 2024 onboarding workshop

The early workshop considered a single global onboarding queue and a forty-five-day migration window. Participants included regional operations, merchant support, and finance control representatives. The proposal was abandoned after data-residency analysis showed that regional sequencing was necessary.

## Gateway naming history

Before the Atlas name was approved, planning slides called the gateway Aurora and sometimes Gateway Next. These aliases refer to exploratory architecture only. No current milestone, budget, or control should be inferred from the old labels.

## Initial payment-provider estimate

The provider originally estimated five days for certification support and suggested reusing an earlier token profile. Architecture reviewers did not accept that profile because required claims were missing. This estimate predates the later contract changes described in the authoritative dossier.

## Retired recovery reserve

Finance once held a planning reserve of USD 150,000 for gateway contingency work. It was a provisional amount, not an approved recovery ceiling. Later council records superseded the reserve, but it remains here to test whether retrieval distinguishes historical values from current decisions.

## Dashboard prototype notes

The first Beacon prototype used weekly spreadsheet extracts and a local visualization package. It had no operational freshness objective and was never exposed to customers. The production-oriented dashboard later adopted event tables and a daily review process.

## Marketing taxonomy experiment

Beacon evaluated a revised marketing taxonomy during a two-week experiment. The taxonomy feed arrived on schedule and did not block the operational dashboard. Workshop attendees nevertheless discussed it often, which made it prominent in several nonauthoritative meeting summaries.

## Knowledge pilot alternatives

The Cygnus team compared keyword-only search, a dense-only prototype, and a manually curated FAQ. Reviewers rejected each as the sole production approach. The approved pilot later combined retrieval methods and added explicit ranking and answer controls.

## Early citation design

An early user-interface mockup displayed a source name without the supporting passage. Support reviewers found that insufficient for quality review. The final design requires document-grounded answers to carry evidence that can be inspected.

## Obsolete authorization target

A 2024 capacity exercise assumed a forty-minute authorization recovery target. The exercise did not become an operating standard. Current objectives are maintained in the reliability manual and may be shorter than values found in historical exercises.

## Settlement replay workshop

Operators once proposed replaying exports immediately after a failed transfer. The proposal was rejected because partial delivery could create duplicates. The later procedure added an integrity check before any replay begins.

## Backup vendor evaluation

The infrastructure group tested two snapshot vendors and one native database mechanism. Cost and restore consistency varied across the trial. Vendor evaluation scores do not define the approved snapshot frequency, retention period, or restore cadence.

## Traffic management simulation

A simulation explored protective thresholds at seventy-five, eighty, and eighty-five percent utilization. Results informed later policy but none of the simulated values automatically became the operating threshold. The approved start and recovery conditions appear in the reliability manual.

## Incident update experiment

Communications tested twenty-minute and forty-five-minute draft cadences in a tabletop exercise. Participants preferred predictable updates over frequent speculation. The exercise record is not the source of the current public update interval.

## Rollback discussion

Several teams proposed latency-only automatic rollback, but reviewers worried about unnecessary reversions during harmless network variation. The approved policy uses sustained error rate and confirmed financial corruption as automatic conditions, while latency remains an investigation signal.

## Identity review migration

Identity Governance migrated review evidence from spreadsheets into the identity platform. During migration, a quarterly template appeared in the same folder as privileged-access reviews. That shared location never changed the more frequent production privilege cadence.

## Emergency access prototype

The first emergency-access prototype issued ninety-minute credentials without an incident reference. Security rejected it. The approved process shortened access, required an incident identifier, and added next-business-day review.

## Retrieval injection exercise

Red-team exercises placed fake instructions in otherwise legitimate documents. Examples requested secret export, permission expansion, and deletion tools. The exercise established that retrieved prose is data to analyze and cannot grant execution authority.

## Evaluation retention proposal

An early proposal retained generated benchmark reports for one year. Storage and privacy review reduced that duration in the approved handbook while keeping fixed benchmark assets under version control. Historical proposal dates must not be reported as current requirements.

## Exception tracking migration

Old exception tickets lacked consistent expiration fields. Governance introduced named ownership, compensating controls, risk approval, and fixed expiry as mandatory data. Continuing operation after expiry is not an implicit renewal.

## Supplier maintenance trial

One trial used a shared supplier account in a segregated sandbox. The approach was not approved for ongoing access. Current supplier accounts are individual, time-bounded, and limited to contracted services.

## Program closeout retrospective

Prior programs closed when feature development ended, leaving operational work unresolved. Northstar therefore includes stabilization, evidence retention, incident resolution, and ownership handoff in closeout criteria. Historical completion practices are not acceptable substitutes.
